name: Lura
vendor: Lura Project (Linux Foundation), started as the KrakenD framework

foundation.via: A series of LF Projects, LLC, donated by KrakenD

summary: A Go framework for building stateless API gateways that fan one client request out to several backends and merge, filter and reshape their responses; the engine inside the KrakenD API Gateway.
intro: Lura is a set of Go packages, not a ready-to-run gateway. You describe the gateway in a JSON file: each entry under `endpoints` is a path and method that clients call, with a list of `backend` requests behind it, each with its own hosts and `url_pattern`. The `config` package parses that file, the `router` package exposes the endpoints over HTTP through an adapter for gin, `net/http`’s mux, chi, gorilla, httptreemux or negroni, and the `proxy` package turns each incoming request into one or more backend calls. Proxies and middlewares are plain functions stacked on each other: `merging` calls several backends concurrently and joins their responses within a timeout, `concurrent` sends duplicate requests and keeps the first good answer, `balancing` picks a host, and an `EntityFormatter` applies each backend’s `allow` and `deny` field lists and `mapping` renames.

That makes Lura a backend-for-frontend builder: a mobile screen that needed four calls to four services can call one gateway endpoint and receive only the fields it uses. The framework is stateless, and KrakenD describes the result as nodes that run independently, “without any coordination or centralized persistence”, so instances scale out behind a load balancer. KrakenD’s Community Edition, also Apache 2.0, assembles Lura with KrakenD’s own components into a binary that adds features such as JWT and OAuth checks, CORS and multi-layer rate limiting; the Lura README sends anyone who wants a complete gateway there. Lura v3.0.0, tagged on September 30, 2026, moved the configuration format to version 4, and KrakenD CE 3.0 is built on it.
strengths: Aggregation is the core feature, not an add-on: one endpoint can call several backends in parallel and return a merged, trimmed response
Stateless and configured by a single file, so every instance is identical and scaling out means starting more of them
Everything is pluggable: proxies and middlewares are small Go functions, so you can embed it in your own program or swap the HTTP router
Vendor-neutral home for the engine behind KrakenD, a gateway the company says ran on more than a million servers a month when it was donated in 2021
limits: A library, not a product: on its own it lacks the authentication, rate limiting and other features KrakenD layers on top, and you need Go to build anything with it
Development is led by KrakenD’s team, which formed the initial Technical Steering Committee, and releases are infrequent: v2.13.0 in October 2025, v2.14 in March 2026, v3.0.0 in September 2026
HTTP only in the router layer: adapters for other protocols such as gRPC, AMQP or NATS are listed as roadmap items
JSON is the only well-tested configuration format; the parser accepts others through viper, but the docs warn they haven’t been tested as much

story: Front ends built on microservices often need data from several services that were not designed around any one screen, so clients made many calls and threw most of each response away. KrakenD, whose team is led by CEO Albert Lombarte, answered that with a gateway that aggregates and trims responses, and has run in production at large internet businesses since 2016. The framework’s stated rules: reactive is key, fail fast rather than succeed slowly, keep it simple, make everything pluggable, and give each request its own context.

On May 11, 2021 the Linux Foundation announced it would host the open-source core as the Lura Project, with partners including Postman, 99P Labs, Ardan Studios, Hepsiburada, Openroom, Skalena and Stayforlong; its technical charter had been adopted on April 14. KrakenD kept its Community and Enterprise editions, made Lura the engine of KrakenD 2.0, and its team became the project’s initial Technical Steering Committee. Lombarte said that week that KrakenD was running on 1.8 million servers.
Lura followed the 2.x line for five years, and v3.0.0 was tagged on September 30, 2026, with KrakenD CE 3.0 built on it.

choices.why: The problem KrakenD set out to solve was clients making many calls to services not shaped for them, so merging and filtering backend responses is built into the proxy layer rather than added as a plug-in.

choices.choice: Stateless, with configuration in one file
choices.why: With no shared state or database, every instance behaves the same and the gateway scales by adding instances.

choices.choice: A library of small components rather than one product
choices.why: Following the Unix philosophy, Lura offers reusable pieces that can be assembled into different gateways, while KrakenD ships the assembled product.
